sources.note: Index of 427 SIL Cameroon files; none is named for Laimbwe/Laimbue. Only concerns the language; Weh and Aghem (Thormoset MA thesis) phonologies exist for neighbouring West Ring languages.

sources.citation: Troyer, Duane, Paul Huey & Joseph Mbongue. 1995. A rapid appraisal survey of Mmen (ALCAM 821) and Aghem dialects (ALCAM 810), Menchum Division, North-West Province. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 20 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only document Glottolog attaches to Laimbue; a sociolinguistic survey with wordlists that may carry tone marks and a remark on prosody; would at least settle whether SIL recorded any phonological notes. Internet Archive copy exists (silcam.org/documents/, 2016-06-15) but web.archive.org was could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. (ed.). Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: Laimbue. Data provided by Dr. Henry K. Kah (Laimbue speaker), written out by Dr. Pius W. Akumbu (University of Buea), 5 Nov 2012.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about stress. Numerals 1-2000 are transcribed with tone diacritics (e.g. mòʔ '1', táì '5', sùmbô '7', ìfámá '8', bə́lə́mɔ̀ʔ '9', ɨɣɨ́m '10', fə́fú '100', kám '1000'), i.e. the only primary Laimbue data found are tone-marked; no prose on accent.
